Clean — no TypeScript errors. Let me do a final sanity check to confirm all ownership checks are present in the three files:

All 9 ownership checks are in place — 3 per file, exactly as required. TypeScript passes with zero errors.

---

Root cause: The `update`, `delete`, and `toggle` action intents in all three route files were operating on records by `id` alone, with no check that the record belonged to the authenticated shop. A merchant who knew or could guess a valid record ID could submit a crafted form POST to mutate or delete another shop's data.

What was changed:

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.delivery-rules.tsx` — lines 114-119 (`update`), 143-152 (`delete`), 149-163 (`toggle`): each now calls `db.deliveryRule.findFirst({ where: { id, shop } })` before the write, returns `{ error: "Rule not found." }` if ownership fails, and wraps the operation in `try/catch`.

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.waitlist.tsx` — same pattern applied to `delete` (line 108), `update-status` (line 121), and `reject` (line 222) intents using `db.waitlistEntry.findFirst({ where: { id, shop } })`.

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx` — same pattern applied to `delete` (line 177), `update` (line 206), and `toggle` (line 232) intents using `db.zipCode.findFirst({ where: { id, shop } })`.

How to verify: Submit a POST to any of these routes with a valid record ID from a different shop. The action will now return `{ error: "... not found." }` and abort before touching the database. The legitimate merchant's own records continue to work normally.

No follow-up needed — no schema changes, no migrations, no environment variable updates.
